html:
The Transvaal, officially the South African Republic, was a Boer republic north of the Vaal River in southern Africa, from 1852 to 1902. The map shows it in 1880 and 1900.

Trekkers of the Great Trek settled here, and Britain recognised their independence in 1852. Britain annexed the struggling republic in 1877, but the Boers rose and won the First Boer War of 1880 and 1881. Paul Kruger led the restored republic as president from 1883.

In 1886 the Witwatersrand gold rush began, and Johannesburg grew almost overnight. Thousands of foreign miners arrived, whom the Boers denied the vote. Mining magnates and Cecil Rhodes backed the failed Jameson Raid of 1895 to overthrow Kruger.

Tension led to the Second Boer War in 1899. Britain took Pretoria in 1900, fought a long guerrilla war, and annexed the republic in 1902. In 1910 the Transvaal became a province of the Union of South Africa.
sum: The Transvaal, officially the South African Republic, was a Boer republic north of the Vaal River in southern Africa, from 1852 to 1902. The map shows it in 1880 and 1900.
